candidates.title: C1 — README hero still imports dattri.task + functional_call
candidates.evidence_paper: §3.3 / Abstract: live capture from any `.backward()` including DDP/FSDP; closed-loop Attributor over live model.
candidates.evidence_code: README.md:33,144 `from dattri.task import AttributionTask`; hero loss_fn(params, batch)+functional_call. Contrasts dattri_llm/task.py (model,batch) contract and examples/attribution/attribution_on_the_fly.py.
candidates.proposed_fix: Replace both README snippets with `from dattri_llm import AttributionTask` (or `from dattri_llm.task import …`) and a `(model, batch) -> loss` that calls the live model; mention `AttributionTask.from_dattri` as the adapter for dattri-style losses.
candidates.why_effective: Highest-traffic copy-paste path still contradicts the paper's distributed/live-hook story and the library's own task contract.

candidates.title: C5 — examples README marks on_the_fly as needing transformers
candidates.evidence_paper: N/A (docs). Paper 'few lines' framing assumes minimal deps for basic attribution.
candidates.evidence_code: examples/README.md table: attribution_on_the_fly → `transformers`. Script uses only torch + dattri_llm MLP; CI still installs transformers before running it.
candidates.proposed_fix: Change Extra requirements to `—` (torch-only). Optionally add a one-line note that live HF/LLM demos need `.[transformers]`.
candidates.why_effective: False barrier; users think the smallest end-to-end demo needs HF when it does not.

candidates.title: C2 — README install omits trl / olmo / dev extras

candidates.proposed_fix: Extend install subsection with `.[trl]`, `.[olmo]`, `.[dev]` (and `.[test]`) one-liners pointing at examples/trainers/*.

candidates.proposed_fix: Add a short 'Custom / HF norm layers' subsection (or link) showing LlamaRMSNorm → nn.RMSNorm declaration with rms_norm_module_kwargs(variance_epsilon=…).
candidates.why_effective: Llama/Qwen users hit unrecognized RMSNorm classes; the fix exists but is buried.

candidates.title: W1 — Abstract 'and and'

candidates.evidence_code: N/A (paper-only).

candidates.title: I1 — Curvature speedup 1.3–2.5× (abstract) vs 1.4–3.1× (body)

candidates.evidence_code: experiments/benchmark/{throughput,routing,benchmark}.py measure cells; do not encode abstract range.
candidates.proposed_fix: Reconcile abstract to one audited table slice (or qualify 'vs fastest baseline on completed projected-curvature cells').

candidates.title: I2 — 'gradient similarity at parity' vs GradDot 2.7–3.4× / 1.4–8.9×
candidates.evidence_paper: Abstract: 'gradient similarity at parity.' §4: GradDot achieves 2.7–3.4× Kronfluence and 1.4–8.9× Bergson on completed scales.
candidates.evidence_code: experiments/benchmark/throughput.py; README maps Grad-Dot → TracInAttributor.
candidates.proposed_fix: Replace 'at parity' with the measured range, or define parity as a specific matched-hardware row and move the × gains into the same sentence.

candidates.evidence_paper: 'we will introduct in §3.2'; Related Work 'building blocks motivates'; repeated 'Eq. equation 1/2/3/4' and 'Equation equation 1' (A.1); A.3 'moments the coming optimizer.step()'.
candidates.evidence_code: N/A.
candidates.proposed_fix: introduct→introduce; motivates→motivate; fix equation refs to 'Eq. (N)'; repair 'moments the coming' grammar.
